newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Chamber of Commerce confidence index declines.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Chamber of Commerce confidence index declines.

text.p: The U.S. Chamber of Commerce Business Confidence Index dropped to its lowest level in 18 months in December, the group said Friday.
Based on a bi-monthly survey charting the outlook for economic growth, employment and sales, the index was down 1.2 points from October to 52.3.

"Businesses continue to anticipate a lackluster year in 1997," said Chamber chief economist economist Martin Regalia. "Concern about consumer spending and the federal govenment's ability to deal with pressing economic problems continue to weigh heavily on the business outlook."
Businesses tended to be more optimistic about sales and employment prospects for their own companies than about the economy in general, the survey showed.
The index stood at 52.2 in June 1995.
